subject.title: Discord routing: mention > reply-target > default owner (suppress default owner when targeted)

question: Should Discord adopt strict active-target precedence that suppresses the default owner whenever a message explicitly mentions another configured bot or replies to another configured bot's message?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but the fix changes stable Discord multi-bot routing and can intentionally stop default-owner traffic that existing deployments may currently receive.

options.title: Adopt Strict Precedence
options.body: Implement Discord-owned mention > reply-target > default-owner selection with default-owner suppression, focused tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Split The Semantics
options.body: Keep this issue open as the strict-precedence tracker while narrower issues and PRs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80234 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80235 handle only bot-authored reply activation.

options.title: Keep Current Default Routing
options.body: Document static default-owner routing plus existing `ignoreOtherMentions` behavior as the supported contract and close or narrow cross-bot suppression requests that conflict with it.

recommendation.title: Adopt Strict Precedence
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned mention > reply-target > default-owner selection with default-owner suppression, focused tests, and live Discord proof.
